title: Monthly Payout for ComCare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance Recipients
what_it_is: Monthly Payout for ComCare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance Recipients

sections.label: SMTA household numbers and assistance
sections.summary: Between 2015 and 2017, 14,000 to 16,000 households received SMTA, with median monthly assistance of about $400 over about six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2017, the number of households that received SMTA at any point in time was between 14,000 and 16,000 households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We do not have readily available data on how many of these were first-time SMTA applicants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The median monthly assistance quantum that a household on SMTA received was about $400 and the median duration of assistance in a year was about six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Among households whose SMTA ended in 2016, about 25% households reapplied and received SMTA within 12 months.

sections.label: SG Cares Community Networks and hubs
sections.summary: SG Cares Community Networks were announced to integrate Government and people sector support, with hubs planned in rental housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Member may be aware that last year, we announced efforts to develop, all across the island, SG Cares Community Networks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We seek to integrate the support that all these organisations – both Government and people sector – can provide so that we can give more holistic assistance to families, especially those who face complex needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also announced last year our intentions to launch hubs in rental housing estates so that we can bring together the agencies and the Voluntary Welfare Organisations (VWOs) that have been working very intimately and closely with families living in rental housing.

sections.label: Assessing appropriate assistance duration
sections.summary: SSOs and agencies such as Family Service Centres assess families' needs holistically to decide the appropriate duration of assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On the Member's second point, I think what he meant was whether we should consider increasing the duration as opposed to what he said, "reducing the duration".

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There are some families whose needs may be more short-term, for example, they may need, say, two to three months of assistance before they transit to a new job which they can secure with or without assistance; or they may require longer-term assistance because they may be undergoing more structural training, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The SSOs, together with our agencies, such as Family Service Centres, would assess the needs of the families holistically, and then make the necessary decisions as to what that appropriate duration would be.
